brief:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham acknowledged that his government previously refrained from acting against Israeli occupation policies, fearing accusations of antisemitism, according to Shehab Wire. The admission came as the government signaled a departure from years of caution on the contentious matter.

Burnham disclosed that officials had worried such action would expose the administration to charges of antisemitism, a concern that had deterred policy intervention. The hesitation reflected broader sensitivities surrounding criticism of Israeli actions within British political discourse and public debate.

The government has now resolved to intensify diplomatic and political pressure on Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank, marking a shift toward a more assertive stance on the occupation and the settlement enterprise.
